title: Decision Compression
hook: By 3pm I can't even decide what to eat. Too many small calls before lunch.
statement: Cut down the choices you face so your best thinking goes to the decisions that matter.
explainer: Every open decision pulls from the same tank of mental energy. Decide repeat stuff once, in advance, and save your judgment for calls that actually change outcomes.
sop: List every decision you make more than 3 times a week.
Turn the top 5 into defaults: a uniform, a meal rotation, a reply template.
Each morning, rate your Energy and count your open decisions, your Load.
Protect one 15-minute block for real judgment calls only.
Review monthly and drop defaults that stopped fitting.
equation_example: Energy is 7 out of 10, and your Load is 14 open decisions. 7 ÷ 14 = 0.5. Closer to 1 or above means each decision gets your full attention. Lower means you're spread thin and quality slips.
question: Name the recurring decision that drains you most, and write the default that replaces it.
closing_statement: Default the repeatable. Save judgment for what isn't.
